method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the ASHM HIV page. No antiretroviral regimen is asserted, because the source names none; those gaps are recorded as input_unavailable rather than filled from model memory.

claims.claim: Untreated HIV causes chronic immune deficiency which can progress to AIDS after a variable period of 2-20 years but on average 10 years after infection
claims.source_text: Untreated infection with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) causes chronic immune deficiency which can progress to acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) after a variable period (2-20 years) but on average 10 years after infection.

claims.claim: Combination antiretroviral therapy is lifelong and should start as soon as possible after diagnosis regardless of CD4+ T-cell count
claims.source_text: People with HIV are treated by combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) which is life long and should start as soon as possible after diagnosis regardless of CD4+ T-cell count.

claims.claim: Consider starting ART at the time of diagnosis or as soon as possible following diagnosis, regardless of CD4+ T-cell count
claims.source_text: Consider starting ART at the time of diagnosis or as soon as possible following diagnosis, regardless of CD4+ T-cell count.

claims.claim: People with HIV who consistently take ART daily as prescribed and achieve and maintain an undetectable viral load cannot sexually transmit the virus to an HIV-negative partner and have a near normal life expectancy
claims.source_text: People with HIV who consistently take ART daily as prescribed and who achieve and maintain an undetectable HIV viral load cannot sexually transmit the virus to an HIV-negative partner (U=U, undetectable = untransmissible) and have a near normal life expectancy.

claims.claim: Post-exposure prophylaxis can be offered within 72 hours of potential HIV exposure
claims.source_text: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) can be offered within 72 hours of potential HIV exposure.

claims.claim: If there is potential for transmission within the last 72 hours, such as condomless sex, offer post-exposure prophylaxis to that contact
claims.source_text: If there is potential for transmission within the last 72 hours (e.g. condomless sex), offer post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to that contact.

claims.claim: A confirmatory test following a reactive HIV self-test must be completed
claims.source_text: People may present following a reactive HIV self-test. A confirmatory test following a reactive HIV self-test must be completed.

claims.claim: Acute HIV infection is symptomatic in 70% of patients with fever, rash, lymphadenopathy, pharyngitis, myalgia and diarrhoea, and the seroconversion illness often occurs about 2 weeks after exposure
claims.source_text: Acute infection (symptomatic in 70% of patients): fever, rash, lymphadenopathy, pharyngitis, myalgia, diarrhoea. This seroconversion illness often occurs about 2 weeks after exposure.

claims.claim: Asymptomatic infection can occur for several years following infection
claims.source_text: Asymptomatic infection: can then occur for several years following infection.

claims.claim: HIV is transmitted through contact with blood, semen or anogenital fluid from a person with a detectable viral load, entering through a mucous membrane of the rectum, vagina or tip of penis, open wounds or direct injection
claims.source_text: HIV is transmitted when someone is in contact with body fluids (blood, semen, anogenital fluid) from a person with HIV who has a detectable viral load. These fluids must enter a HIV-negative person through a mucous membrane (rectum/vagina/tip of penis), open wounds or direct injection.

claims.claim: HIV can be transmitted vertically if the pregnant person has a detectable viral load during pregnancy or when breastfeeding
claims.source_text: HIV can also be transmitted vertically if the pregnant person has a detectable viral load during pregnancy or when breastfeeding.

claims.claim: Discuss the support available for all newly diagnosed patients, including peer navigation for people wanting to find support, information or services
claims.source_text: Discuss support available for all newly diagnosed patients. This includes peer navigation for people wanting to find support, information or services.

claims.claim: Urgent referral to an experienced counsellor or psychologist may be needed
claims.source_text: May need urgent referral to experienced counsellor or psychologist.

claims.claim: Avoid overemphasis of technical discussions about treatment options in the initial discussion
claims.source_text: Avoid overemphasis of technical discussions about treatment options in the initial discussion.

claims.claim: Consider completing comprehensive STI testing for syphilis, chlamydia and gonorrhoea if not undertaken at first presentation, or retesting post the window period
claims.source_text: Consider completing comprehensive STI testing (syphilis, chlamydia, gonorrhoea), if not undertaken at first presentation, or retesting post the window period.

claims.claim: Notify the state or territory health department
claims.source_text: Notify the state or territory health department.

claims.claim: If the patient is unwell, consider urgent referral to hospital or a specialist centre for assessment, and all complex situations should be managed in collaboration with a specialist
claims.source_text: Patient unwell - consider urgent referral to hospital or specialist centre for assessment. All complex situations should be managed in collaboration with a specialist.

claims.claim: HIV primary illness requires urgent commencement of ART
claims.source_text: HIV primary illness | Urgent commencement of ART

claims.claim: CD4 below 200 cells per microlitre is high risk for opportunistic infection and needs urgent treatment, and may need chemoprophylaxis with co-trimoxazole or fluconazole with specialist advice
claims.source_text: CD4 < 200 cells/uL | High risk for opportunistic infection needs urgent treatment. May need chemoprophylaxis with co-trimoxazole/fluconazole - seek specialist advice.

claims.claim: Check HLA-B57 status before use of abacavir
claims.source_text: Allergy to treatment | Check HLA-B57 status before use of abacavir

claims.claim: In pregnancy the patient should start ART and specialist advice should be sought
claims.source_text: Pregnancy | Should start ART. Seek specialist advice

claims.claim: Co-infection with hepatitis B or hepatitis C may need modification of treatment choice with specialist advice
claims.source_text: Co-infection with hepatitis B or hepatitis C | May need to modify treatment choice. Seek specialist advice

claims.claim: AIDS complications include opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia, oesophageal candidiasis and cerebral toxoplasmosis, and cancers such as Kaposi sarcoma
claims.source_text: AIDS: opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis (carinii) jiroveci pneumonia, oesophageal candidiasis, cerebral toxoplasmosis and cancers such as Kaposi sarcoma.

claims.claim: People with HIV are at increased risk for cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, osteoporosis and some non-AIDS malignancies
claims.source_text: Non-infectious comorbidities: people with HIV are at increased risk for cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, osteoporosis and some non-AIDS malignancies.

claims.claim: HIV is a notifiable condition and contact tracing is important to prevent re-infection and reduce transmission
claims.source_text: Notifiable condition. Contact tracing is important to prevent re-infection and reduce transmission.

claims.claim: The diagnosing doctor is responsible for initiating and documenting a discussion about contact tracing
claims.source_text: The diagnosing doctor is responsible for initiating and documenting a discussion about contact tracing.

claims.claim: Contact tracing starts with recent sexual or needle-sharing partners, with an outer limit of the onset of risk behaviour or the last known negative HIV test result if known
claims.source_text: Start with recent sexual or needle-sharing partners; outer limit is onset of risk behaviour or last known negative HIV test result if known.

claims.claim: Close follow-up within a few days of diagnosis is recommended to check psychosocial wellbeing, review baseline investigations and assess response to ART if started
claims.source_text: Close follow-up is recommended after diagnosis, within a few days to check on psychosocial wellbeing, to review baseline investigation and to assess response to ART if started.

claims.claim: The patient needs long-term regular review by a practitioner experienced in HIV care at a specialist clinic, sexual health service or s100 GP prescriber, and should also see their GP for ongoing primary care
claims.source_text: Patient will need long-term regular reviews by a practitioner experienced in HIV care: at a specialist clinic, sexual health service or s100 GP prescriber. Patient should also see their GP for ongoing primary care.

claims.claim: Once stable on ART follow-up can be every 3-6 months
claims.source_text: Once stable on ART follow-up can be every 3-6 months.

claims.claim: Auditable outcomes are that 100% of patients should have contact tracing performed and 100% should be offered treatment at the time of diagnosis
claims.source_text: 100% of patients should have contact tracing performed. 100% of patients should be offered treatment at the time of diagnosis.

claims.claim: Pre-exposure prophylaxis can provide highly effective biomedical prevention of HIV in HIV-negative people
claims.source_text: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is an important new prevention option and can provide highly effective biomedical prevention of HIV in HIV-negative people.

claims.claim: The source directs prescribers to the ASHM Antiretroviral Guidelines and to a list of HIV s100 prescribers rather than naming regimens
claims.source_text: See list of HIV s100 prescribers in your local area. See the Antiretroviral Guidelines for more information about treatment options.

claims.claim: HIV is caused by the human immunodeficiency virus, a single-stranded RNA virus
claims.source_text: Infection with the human immunodeficiency virus, a single-stranded RNA virus.

claims.claim: Immune deficiency produces symptoms related to declining CD4 T-cell count such as oral thrush, diarrhoea, weight loss, skin infections and herpes zoster
claims.source_text: Immune deficiency: multiple symptoms related to declining CD4 T-cell count such as oral thrush, diarrhoea, weight loss, skin infections, herpes zoster.

claims.claim: All patients need regular monitoring visits to assess immune status, check response to therapy and provide psychosocial support
claims.source_text: All patients need regular monitoring visits to assess their immune status, to check on response to therapy and to provide psychosocial support.
